brief: Fix Q-exact-sections in dwitbuk.py only: the diff composed from candidate paths (path_diff, used by the eyes request's diff and verify_packet's excluded_diff) must hold, for each kept candidate, that path's own diff section exactly once and nothing else — a literal pathspec :(literal)N still reaches N/child when N changed between file and directory, so do not rely on pathspec magic to separate them. Either keep only the sections of git's output whose path is one of the batch's kept names (git's diff --git headers are repository-root relative while the candidates are target-relative via --relative, and git C-quotes unusual names in headers — handle both), or isolate such a name with exclusions taken from git's own candidate listing; whichever you choose, the text without any file/directory change stays exactly what one unbatched call gives (the existing batching, rename, subdirectory-target and ARG_MAX tests hold it). Keep everything else as it is: is_record, PATHSPEC_BATCH_BYTES, an oversized path alone in its own call, --no-renames, untracked directories skipped, the gitlink marker, mangsang/ handling. test_dwitbuk.py is the contract and protected: do not edit it, hooks/stop_eyes.py, README.md, the manifests, eyes_worker.py or hostcall.py, and do not commit. Run the suite with AGENT_WORKER unset (env -u AGENT_WORKER python3 test_dwitbuk.py): inside a worker session test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else fails only because that hook steps aside when AGENT_WORKER=1.

built.summary: Updated only dwitbuk.py: path_diff filters each batch to exact candidate sections, handling repository-relative and C-quoted headers. All tests passed; protected files remain unchanged.

xs-tests: Item 2 ('Without such a file/directory change the text is what it was: one unbatched call over the kept paths') is checked only inside the batch-boundary test's second half (an eyes request from the directory commit, with the lowered limit) and by the existing batching test. No separate test checks excluded_diff without a file/directory change against one unbatched call.

Items (4) and (5) ('a single path longer than PATHSPEC_BATCH_BYTES is diffed (alone) rather than refused, dropped or raised on'; 'a gitlink inside a nested repository that the traversal walks into is marked like one at the top level') pass on the current tree by design. They were shown failing only against one-site mutant copies (path_diff skips or raises on an oversized path; gitlinks marked only at the top level). No other way of breaking them was tried.

The exact-sections rule is checked on three cases: a file replaced by a directory, a staged child, and a lowered batch limit at the foo / foo/a.py boundary. It is not checked for a target inside a larger repository, nested repositories in verify_packet's touched diff, or past the 80000/40000-character cuts.
'Findings 7 and 9 of the first review stay documented limits.' This is about what the documentation says, and no test decides it.

Already failing before my change, and not caused by it: test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else fails with JSONDecodeError in this session, and fails the same way with HEAD's test_dwitbuk.py. The check `python3 test_dwitbuk.py` will keep failing until that test passes, whatever the build does.
